original_request: Find the community button on the sample browser and separate it to turn it into a new Chat implementation. Study, plan and present in ASCII mockups the best way to turn that into a chat, including the plan of what we need to add to license_server. Present the entire plan first.

enhanced_specification.title: Community Chat System - Native In-App Real-Time Chat
enhanced_specification.summary: Transform the existing Community button in SampleBrowserPage from a web browser redirect into a native JUCE chat component with real-time messaging capabilities. This involves creating a new ChatPage component for SAMPLAR, adding WebSocket/REST API endpoints to the license_server, and implementing message storage in PostgreSQL.
deliverables: ChatPage.h/.cpp - New native JUCE chat component (replacing or alongside CommunityPage)
ChatService.* - SAMPLAR client service for WebSocket connections and message handling
license_server/plugins/chat_service/ - New chat plugin for backend
Database schema additions for chat_messages, chat_rooms, and chat_users tables
REST API endpoints for message history and user presence

ui_changes: Message list with sender info and timestamps
Text input field with send button
backend_additions: User authentication via existing JWT system

out_of_scope: File sharing/image uploads (can be added later)
Private messaging (focus on community chat first)
assumptions: Use existing JWT authentication from license system
WebSocket library available (JUCE supports raw sockets, may need wrapper)
PostgreSQL database already deployed on Render.com
Users have existing accounts in the license system
Single global chat room initially (can expand to multiple rooms later)
